names_added: uRaw (uniform float, GL_HEAD): volume sampling; with uFlat on, the program writes vec4(surface colour, distance) only
gFade (global float, GL_HEAD): set before a query; an orbit point with step it counts with weight clamp(gFade + 1 - it, 0, 1); 1e9 = everything
gPix (global float, GL_HEAD): set before a query; size of a picture pixel at the point asked about; 0 in the 2D view and for uRaw
gOnTrap (global bool, GL_HEAD): after a query, true when the distance returned is the trap solid's and not the set's
TRAP_THIN (const float 2.0, GL_ORBIT): trap solid layers thinner than this many picture pixels fade out
TRAP_SOLIDS (const bool true, GL_ORBIT): write 'TRAP_SOLIDS = false' into the source to build a program with no trap solid code
PH_CUT (GL_TAIL): new step of main(), one query at the cut face point so its colour reads that point's own orbit
PH_COUNT (GL_TAIL): new step of main(), learns the hit's smooth step count before the colour query
PH_* and END_* constants renumbered: PH_PROBE 0, PH_MARCH 1, PH_SLOPE 2, PH_SHADOW 3, PH_CUT 4, PH_AO 5, PH_COUNT 6, PH_COLOUR 7, END_MISS 8, END_CUT 9, END_LIT 10, END_FLAT 11
TAIL (const float 4.0, GL_TAIL): steps before the end of the orbit that never count towards the trap colour
LEVEL_STEPS (const float 2.0, GL_TAIL): steps added to log(1 / page pixel) / log(power) to get the step a pixel can still resolve
fade, hue, raw (locals of main()): the gFade for the colour query; the step a hit's colour begins with; this pixel is a raw sample
trapOn, tbest (locals of orbitDE): a trap solid is wanted for this query; its distance so far

answers_for_user: The 'set of slices' on the Douady rabbit (N12): it was a bug in the colouring, not in the shape, and it is fixed for the Mandelbrot and Julia pictures. The colour of each point was being read from more steps of its path than one screen pixel can actually show, and the number of steps changed from pixel to pixel, which painted one ring per step. Now only the steps a pixel can show are counted. The rabbit, the Basilica and the default Mandelbrot are smooth at 12, 24 and 60 iterations and at thresholds of 0.2, 1 and 3 pixels. The price: the pictures are calmer, with more blue and green and less yellow and orange than before, and a closer view shows finer colour detail than a far one.

Orbit traps that change the shape (N3): this now works in 3D for Mandelbrot and Julia pictures. The solid can be made from the trap itself, or the trap can be added to the fractal. The sphere shell gives a chain of smooth bubbles, the ring gives linked hoops, the cross gives a spiky sea-urchin, and the point and line give other objects again. It is not yet available in the Kleinian view. At the two fastest quality settings the shapes are complete but most of their colour is lost for now.

The glow around the fractal with the rough estimate (N11): I checked it again on the new trap shapes. There is no glow. At the fastest setting those shapes first came out full of holes; that is fixed.

Colouring the cut face like the 2D inside (N10): the 3D side of this is in place. When you cut the solid open, the colour of the cut face is now read at each point of the face itself, so it matches what the 2D view shows there.

The 2D view: unchanged, checked pixel for pixel on seven different pictures. One deliberate exception: in the 2D mosaic the loud coloured background is gone; each small Julia shape keeps a halo of colour on a plain ground.

Waiting time: with all the new colour options, preparing a new approach or equation now takes about 10 seconds on the test machine where it took about 2. That needs trimming before release, and most of it is in the colour code.
risks: The look of the default pictures changes with the ring cure: fewer steps count, so the shell glow is bluer and flatter (the middle of the default Mandelbrot is a calm blue). The user chose these colours on pictures that had the rings; the colour module's shell radius 1 was tuned to show 'rings and seams'. May need retuning of glow width or radius, or LEVEL_STEPS 3.

answers_for_user: Why the Sphere inversions solid fell apart when you sliced away from z = 0: the version you tested had the planes dial at 2, and that setting folds space before every step. The fold has one seam, the plane y = 0, and the rule jumps across it, which tears the solid everywhere except when c sits on the x-axis. The page now opens with one plane, which has no fold and no jump. Sliced at any height, the solid then comes out as one smooth piece.

Whether the number of planes should be forced: with one plane there is nothing to choose, because one plane is the rule itself, the plain sum of sphere inversions. Two or more planes are now labelled as an earlier version and kept only so you can see the history. In that version the count really is arbitrary: p planes give 2p fins whatever the power is.

What one plane costs: all the fine detail lies around the plane z = 0, and above and below it the surface is smooth and rounded. These are the 'inflated' sets of Figure 3 in Kučera's paper. The spikier, fully 3D look of his Figure 4 is what the two-plane version tried to copy, and that only works for Julia sets whose c is on the x-axis, such as the Basilica. No replacement that looks good everywhere has been found yet.

The Lift dial: pressing play now sweeps it to one end and back, where it used to snap from one end to the other. It slides the detail up and down the solid; it does not make the solid pulse, and its hint no longer says so.

The saved Julia points: every note is now written in plain words, for example 'the round bulb on the left of the Mandelbrot set' where it said 'the period-two disc'. With one plane, three entries look fused until you raise the iterations to about 24. Six of the entries found by exploring were found with the two-plane version and look like plain eggs or copies of other entries until you set Planes to 2. Each of those says so in its note. Nothing was removed.

Extreme ranges: with the switch on, the planes dial goes to 16 (64 if typed), Lift to 6 either way (20 if typed), and the Lathe's spin to 33. The angle dials stay as they are, because an angle just comes back round.
